nodes.summary: For every tree $t$, the arc sequence of $t$ is the Euler tour of $t$ zipped with its own tail: if the Euler tour of $t$ is $v_0, v_1, \dots, v_k$, then the arc sequence of $t$ is $(v_0, v_1), (v_1, v_2), \dots, (v_{k-1}, v_k)$.
nodes.title: Arc sequence as the zipped Euler tour

nodes.summary: The arc sequence of a tree $t$ is the list of consecutive pairs of its Euler tour: if the Euler tour of $t$ is $v_0, v_1, \dots, v_k$, then the arc sequence of $t$ is $(v_0, v_1), (v_1, v_2), \dots, (v_{k-1}, v_k)$.
nodes.title: Arc sequence of the Euler tour

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a property of trees. Suppose that for every vertex $r$ and all trees $c_1, \dots, c_k$ (with $k \ge 0$), if $P$ holds for each $c_i$, then $P$ holds for the tree with root $r$ and child subtrees $c_1, \dots, c_k$. Then $P$ holds for every tree.
nodes.title: Induction principle for rooted trees

nodes.summary: The children of a tree are the child subtrees of its root, as a list in their given order.
nodes.title: Children of a rooted tree

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a tree with root $r$ and child subtrees $c_1, \dots, c_k$. Cutting the last child subtree of $t$ gives no result when $k = 0$; when $k \ge 1$ it gives the pair consisting of the tree with root $r$ and child subtrees $c_1, \dots, c_{k-1}$, together with the removed subtree $c_k$.
nodes.title: Cutting the last child subtree

nodes.summary: Let $t_1$ be a tree with root $r$ and child subtrees $c_1, \dots, c_k$, and let $t_2$ be a tree. The link of $t_1$ and $t_2$ is the tree with root $r$ and child subtrees $c_1, \dots, c_k, t_2$, so $t_2$ becomes the new last child subtree of the root of $t_1$.
nodes.title: Linking two rooted trees

nodes.summary: For every tree $t$ and every $v$, $v$ occurs in the Euler tour of $t$ if and only if $v$ is a vertex of $t$.
nodes.title: The Euler tour visits exactly the vertices of the tree

nodes.summary: For every vertex $r$, the link of the single-vertex tree with root $r$ and another single-vertex tree with root $r$ is not valid, since the vertex $r$ occurs twice in it. Hence the link of two valid trees need not be valid when their vertex sets are not disjoint.
nodes.title: Linking two copies of a single vertex is not valid

nodes.summary: The root of the tree with root vertex $r$ and child subtrees $c_1, \dots, c_k$ is the vertex $r$.
nodes.title: Root of a rooted tree

nodes.summary: The size of a tree is its number of nodes, counting repeated vertex labels with multiplicity: the tree with root $r$ and child subtrees $c_1, \dots, c_k$ has size $1 + \sum_{i=1}^{k} \operatorname{size}(c_i)$.
nodes.title: Size of a rooted tree

nodes.summary: For lists $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ of vertices and a vertex $r$, the splice of $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ at $r$ is the list consisting of the entries of $\tau_1$, followed by the entries of $\tau_2$, followed by $r$.
nodes.title: Splicing two Euler tours

nodes.summary: For every tree $t$ and every list $a$ of vertices, the Euler tour of $t$ with accumulator $a$ equals the Euler tour of $t$ followed by $a$.
nodes.title: Accumulator lemma for the Euler tour

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a tree with root $r$ and child subtrees $c_1, \dots, c_k$ in order, and let $a$ be a list of vertices. For a list $L$ of vertices, write $r \cdot L$ for the list $L$ with $r$ put in front. The Euler tour of $t$ with accumulator $a$, written $T(t, a)$, is $r \cdot L_1$, where $L_{k+1} = a$ and $L_i = T(c_i, r \cdot L_{i+1})$ for $i = k, \dots, 1$.
nodes.title: Euler tour with an accumulator

nodes.summary: For trees $t_1$ and $t_2$, let $t$ be the link of $t_1$ and $t_2$, that is, $t_1$ with $t_2$ added as the last child subtree of its root. The Euler tour of $t$ is the Euler tour of $t_1$, followed by the Euler tour of $t_2$, followed by the root of $t_1$.
nodes.title: Euler tour of a linked tree

nodes.summary: For a vertex $r$ and a list of trees $c_1, \dots, c_k$, the Euler tour of the tree with root $r$ and child subtrees $c_1, \dots, c_k$ in order is $r$, followed, for each $i = 1, \dots, k$ in turn, by the Euler tour of $c_i$ and then $r$.
nodes.title: Recursive formula for the Euler tour

nodes.summary: The Euler tour of a tree $t$ with root $r$ and child subtrees $c_1, \dots, c_k$ in order is the list of vertices consisting of $r$, followed, for each $i = 1, \dots, k$ in turn, by the Euler tour of $c_i$ and then $r$. It is the vertex sequence of the depth-first walk that returns to the parent vertex after each child subtree.
nodes.title: Euler tour

nodes.summary: A rooted ordered tree with vertices in a type $V$ consists of a root vertex in $V$ together with an ordered list of child subtrees, each a rooted ordered tree with vertices in $V$.
nodes.title: Rooted ordered tree

nodes.summary: A tree $t$ is valid if and only if its list of vertices in preorder has no repeated entries.
nodes.title: Valid trees have distinct vertices

nodes.summary: Let $t_1$ and $t_2$ be valid trees such that no vertex of $t_1$ is a vertex of $t_2$. Then the link of $t_1$ and $t_2$, that is, $t_1$ with $t_2$ added as the last child subtree of its root, is valid.
nodes.title: Linking valid trees with disjoint vertices gives a valid tree

nodes.summary: For every vertex $r$, the tree with root $r$ and no child subtrees is valid.
nodes.title: A single-vertex tree is valid

nodes.summary: A rooted ordered tree is valid when its list of vertices in preorder has no duplicates, that is, every vertex label occurs at most once in the tree.
nodes.title: Valid Euler-tour tree

nodes.summary: For every rooted ordered tree $t$ and every list $a$, the accumulator preorder traversal of $t$ started from $a$ equals the preorder vertex list of $t$ followed by $a$.
nodes.title: Accumulator preorder traversal is append

nodes.summary: For a rooted ordered tree $t$ with root $r$ and child subtrees $c_1, \dots, c_k$ (in order) and a list $a$, the accumulator traversal $T(t, a)$ is the list whose first entry is $r$ and whose remaining entries are $T(c_1, T(c_2, \dots, T(c_k, a) \dots))$; when $k = 0$ the remaining entries are $a$.
nodes.title: Accumulator preorder traversal

nodes.summary: For a vertex $r$ and rooted ordered trees $c_1, \dots, c_k$, the preorder vertex list of the tree with root $r$ and child subtrees $c_1, \dots, c_k$ (in order) is $r$ followed by the concatenation of the preorder vertex lists of $c_1, \dots, c_k$, in this order.
nodes.title: Preorder vertex list of a node

nodes.summary: The preorder vertex list of a rooted ordered tree $t$ is the accumulator preorder traversal of $t$ started from the empty list.
nodes.title: Preorder vertex list of a rooted tree

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
